chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Zurra from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they both said:

Any man who has wealth placed (saved) until a year passes over it, then he must purify it (pay Zakat); and even if there is debt upon him equal to it or more than it, let him purify (pay Zakat) on what is in his hand.
ai.seo_question: Do I pay Zakat on my savings if I have debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that Zakat is obligatory on stored wealth regardless of whether one holds debts equal to or exceeding that wealth, emphasizing the purification of possession over net asset calculation. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that Zakat is a right of God on the wealth itself, distinct from personal liability, ensuring the spiritual cleansing of assets even when heavily indebted. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to maintain religious obligations without being paralyzed by financial liabilities.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, and Zureys from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, both having said:

‘Whichever man who has wealth placed for him until a year passes by over it, so he would be purifying it (paying Zakāt); and even though there may be debts upon him of the likes of it, and more than it. So let him purify (pay Zakāt) on what is in his hands’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from abu Ja‘far and Durays who has said the following:

“Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said, ‘Whoever has an asset that remains with him for one year, he is required to pay its Zakat even if he owes to others an equal amount of asset or more. He is required to pay Zakat for what is in his hand.’”
